headline: Converting blood cells from an 80-year-old into neural stem cells was reported to reset their molecular age to under 20
intervention: Direct conversion of blood cells into neural stem cells
summary: University of Bonn researchers reported that blood cells from an 80-year-old donor, converted into neural stem cells in the laboratory, had a molecular age of under 20. The work was done in cells only. It was presented as a way to study how cells become younger and to understand age-related disease, not as a treatment.
article_title: Rejuvenation breakthrough: Scientists reverse 60 years of aging in human cells

headline: An AI-designed nine-amino-acid peptide, SenoMune-0257, was reported to help the immune system clear senescent cells
indication: Accumulation of senescent cells with age
summary: US company Immorta Bio said its experimental peptide SenoMune-0257 is designed to help the immune system find and remove senescent cells, and that planned preclinical studies are complete. The article notes that safety and effectiveness in people have not been established.
article_title: Is living longer a reality? AI-designed anti-ageing breakthrough could help eliminate ‘zombie cells’
promise: Could enter human evaluation before the end of 2026

headline: An experimental AMPK-activating compound called 991 was reported to extend the lifespan of yeast, worms and flies by up to 25%
summary: UK researchers reported that an experimental compound known as 991, which boosts the energy-sensing protein AMPK, made yeast, worms and flies live up to 25% longer. No mammal was tested. A researcher quoted in the article said the field is still a long way from anti-ageing trials in people.
article_title: UK scientists reveal anti-aging breakthrough as drug is proved to extend life of organisms by 25%

headline: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs were reported by their makers to slow molecular markers of biological ageing
summary: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly reported that their GLP-1 medicines reduced molecular markers of age in patients taking them for weight loss or diabetes. The reports concern ageing markers, not lifespan, and the articles say it is unknown whether healthy people of normal weight would benefit.
article_title: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers
Could GLP-1 drugs be anti-aging medications?

headline: Temporarily removing overactive brain immune cells was reported to restore more than two hours of daily sleep in mice with Alzheimer's-like disease
summary: University of Kentucky researchers reported that overactive immune cells in the brain drive sleep loss in mice with Alzheimer's-like disease. Temporarily removing those cells restored more than two hours of sleep per day without clearing amyloid plaques. The study was in mice.
article_title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques

headline: An antibody blocking the CXCR3 protein was reported to preserve about 40% more memory-centre tissue in mice with tau build-up
indication: Neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease and other tauopathies
summary: Washington University in St. Louis researchers used an antibody against CXCR3, a protein that helps T cells enter the brain, in mice with tau accumulation. Treated mice kept roughly 40% more tissue in memory centres and did better on memory tests, although tau itself was not removed. The work has been done only in mice.
article_title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau

headline: A nanogel called Nano-ERASER was reported to turn brain support cells into neurons and restore memory in mice with Alzheimer's-like disease
summary: University of South Carolina researchers reported in Cell Biomaterials that a polymer nanogel, Nano-ERASER, prompted astrocytes to convert into neurons. It regenerated neurons in human brain organoids, and after two injections mice with Alzheimer's-like symptoms did better at nest-building and a water maze. No person has been treated.
article_title: Nanoparticles shown to reverse memory loss in Alzheimer's breakthrough
Alzheimer's hope: Nanoparticles regenerate cells to restore memory
Scientists invent a gel that creates neurons from other cells, which could help treat Alzheimer's

headline: A nasal spray of extracellular vesicles from amniotic membrane cells was reported to protect brain connections and memory in an animal model of Alzheimer's disease
intervention: Nasal spray of extracellular vesicles from amniotic membrane cells
summary: Researchers at the Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore and partner institutes in Italy gave a nasal spray of extracellular vesicles to an animal model of Alzheimer's disease. It protected connections between brain cells, prevented memory deficits and countered decline that had already begun. The vesicles also protected human neurons grown in the laboratory.
article_title: Could a Nasal Spray Stop Alzheimer’s Before Memory Loss Begins?

headline: B-SYNC CAR-T cells were reported to clear diffuse midline glioma in every mouse treated
summary: University of California, San Francisco researchers engineered CAR-T cells that switch on their cancer-targeting receptors only after entering the brain. The treatment cleared tumours in every mouse across two models of diffuse midline glioma, a childhood brain cancer, and treated mice rejected a second introduction of cancer cells weeks later.
article_title: Breakthrough Cancer Treatment Wipes Out Deadly Brain Tumors in Every Mouse Tested
promise: Human clinical trials could begin as early as April 2027

headline: A personalised mRNA vaccine given with pembrolizumab was reported to cut the risk of melanoma returning or causing death by 42% in a Phase 3 trial
indication: Melanoma at high risk of recurrence after surgery
summary: Moderna and Merck reported Phase 3 results for a vaccine made individually for each patient's tumour and given with the immunotherapy pembrolizumab. The risk of the melanoma returning or of death was 42% lower than with pembrolizumab alone. The vaccine is not yet approved.
article_title: Experimental mRNA vaccine cuts risk melanoma returns by 42%
World-First Cancer Vaccine Cuts Melanoma Recurrence or Death Risk by 42% in Landmark Trial
Personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma cut risk of cancer’s return in late-stage trial
World-first personalised cancer vaccine slashes risk of death and disease returning

headline: The drug sacituzumab tirumotecan was reported to lower the risk of death in a trial in endometrial cancer
summary: A trial of the drug sacituzumab tirumotecan in women with endometrial cancer reported a lower risk of death than with the comparison treatment. The article presents it as a possible new treatment option that is still under study.
article_title: New drug could reduce death risk for women with common cancer
Merck ADC drug cut risk of death by one-third in advanced endometrial cancer

headline: Daily oral vitamin C was reported to be linked to a lower risk of death in people with pre-leukaemia blood disorders in a Phase 2 trial
indication: Pre-leukaemia blood disorders (CCUS and low-risk MDS)
summary: Researchers in Copenhagen and at the Van Andel Institute gave 109 people with pre-leukaemia blood disorders either vitamin C or a placebo in a randomised Phase 2 trial. In an exploratory analysis over three years, the vitamin C group had a 65% lower risk of death. The authors describe themselves as cautiously optimistic.
article_title: A Cheap Daily Vitamin Shows Promise For People at Risk of Leukemia, Early Trial Finds

headline: A comb-shaped electrical stimulation device was reported to regrow most lost hair in mice within about a month
summary: Researchers built a comb-like device that delivers electrical stimulation to the scalp and tested it in mice with induced pattern hair loss. The mice regrew most of their lost hair in about a month, more than with minoxidil. It has not been tested in people.
article_title: Electric Comb Regrows Nearly All Lost Hair in Balding Mice in Just 30 Days
Could this experimental electric comb be a cure for baldness?

headline: A daily oral minoxidil pill, VDPHL01, was reported to increase hair growth in a Phase 3 trial of 536 men with pattern baldness
summary: Veradermics reported results of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial of its daily pill VDPHL01 in 536 men with mild to moderate pattern baldness. Hair growth increased significantly compared with placebo. The company hopes it will become the first oral minoxidil approved by the FDA for hair loss.
article_title: Scientists Tested an Experimental Baldness Pill on 536 Men. Here's What Happened.

headline: Injecting temporary genetic instructions into the heart was reported to improve heart function in mice after a heart attack
intervention: Temporary genetic instructions injected into the heart to activate repair proteins
indication: Heart failure after a heart attack
summary: University of Cambridge researchers reported in Nature Cardiovascular Research that injecting temporary genetic instructions into the heart activated proteins that promote tissue repair. Mice that had suffered heart attacks had a stronger heartbeat and about 10% more blood flow. It has been tested only in mice; the researchers plan to move to larger mammals and then people.
article_title: Scientists suggest new treatment could see hearts repair themselves in major breakthrough

headline: A single dose of the CRISPR therapy CTX310 was reported to roughly halve LDL cholesterol and triglycerides for at least a year in 15 patients
indication: High LDL cholesterol and triglycerides that are hard to treat
summary: A first-in-human trial led by the Cleveland Clinic gave 15 people with severe lipid disorders one infusion of CTX310, which edits the ANGPTL3 gene in the liver. Results in the New England Journal of Medicine showed falls in LDL cholesterol and triglycerides of about 50% at the highest dose that lasted at least a year. The therapy remains experimental.
article_title: An Experimental One-Time Treatment for High Cholesterol Shows Promising Results
One CRISPR treatment cut “bad” cholesterol in half for a full year

headline: A personalised magnetic brain stimulation treatment was reported by its maker to bring 68% of trial patients with PTSD into remission
summary: Wave Neuroscience, working with Texas A&M researchers, received FDA clearance for a treatment that uses measurements of brain activity to guide magnetic stimulation. The company reported a 52% reduction in PTSD symptoms and 68% remission in a clinical trial. The full findings had not been published when the article appeared.
article_title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial

headline: A single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate was reported to ease treatment-resistant depression within a day
summary: A trial published in JAMA tested a single dose of a short-acting psychedelic nasal spray, mebufotenin benzoate, in people whose depression had not responded to standard antidepressants. Symptoms eased quickly after one dose. The short duration of the psychedelic effect is presented as an advantage over psilocybin or LSD, which need hours of supervision.
article_title: Single dose of fast-acting psychedelic nasal spray shows promise for stubborn depression

headline: An intensive diet and exercise programme was reported to put 54% of adults under 45 with type 2 diabetes into remission within six months
intervention: Intensive low-calorie diet with structured exercise
summary: A study reported through the European Association for the Study of Diabetes compared an intensive programme of low-calorie diet and structured exercise with usual care in adults under 45 with type 2 diabetes. After six months 54% of the programme group were in remission, against 4% with usual care.
article_title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months
Can diet and exercise reverse type 2 diabetes? What a new study found

headline: The experimental compound DT-109 was reported to reverse severe fatty liver disease in animals by repairing the gut
summary: Michigan Medicine researchers reported in The Journal of Clinical Investigation that DT-109 reduced harmful gut bacteria, protected the intestinal lining and stopped inflammatory substances reaching the liver. In animal models this reversed MASH, a severe form of fatty liver disease. It has not been tested in people.
article_title: New drug reverses severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut

headline: Engineered gut bacteria that release GLP-1 when blood sugar is high were reported to control diabetes in mice and macaques
intervention: Oral engineered E. coli that senses glucose and releases GLP-1
summary: Researchers in Shanghai engineered a probiotic strain of E. coli to make the hormone GLP-1 only when blood sugar is high. Taken by mouth, it worked in mice and in diabetic macaques with no sign of harm. The article says trials in people are some way off.
article_title: A 'living GLP-1 drug' could revolutionize diabetes treatment

headline: A personalised engineered spinal cord implant from Tel Aviv University was reported to be moving towards a first implant in a person with paralysis
summary: Matricelf, a company using technology developed at Tel Aviv University, and Loewenstein Rehabilitation Medical Center announced that they are preparing for a possible first implant of an engineered spinal cord tissue made from a patient's own cells. No person has received the implant yet.
outlet: American Friends of Tel Aviv University
article_title: Tel Aviv University Breakthrough Moves Closer to Helping People with Spinal Cord Injuries Walk Again

headline: The experimental drug Kamuvudine K-9 was reported to reverse paralysis and vision loss in mice with a multiple sclerosis-like disease
summary: University of Virginia researchers reported in Science Translational Medicine that K-9, a compound derived from an HIV medicine, preserved nerve fibres and their myelin coating in mice. Paralysis and vision loss that had already developed were reversed. The results are preclinical.
article_title: Experimental Drug Could Reverse Multiple Sclerosis Damage

headline: The spinal injection zilganersen was reported to be the first drug approved by the FDA for Alexander disease
summary: The FDA approved zilganersen, an injection into the spinal fluid that lowers production of the GFAP protein, for the rare genetic brain disorder Alexander disease. In a trial of 54 children and adults, motor skills held steady or improved in younger patients, compared with decline without treatment. Side effects included vomiting, back pain and some cases of aseptic meningitis.
article_title: After 30 Years, FDA Approves First-Ever Drug For a Rare Neurological Disorder

headline: An optogenetic gene therapy used with light-stimulating goggles was reported to improve light sensitivity in some blind patients with retinitis pigmentosa
intervention: Optogenetic gene therapy with light-stimulating goggles
summary: In a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine and led by the University of Pittsburgh, ten legally blind adults each received one injection of an algae-derived light-sensing gene in one eye and then wore camera goggles. Light sensitivity improved in several of them and some could find and touch objects. None regained normal sight.
article_title: Optogenetic therapy shows early signs of improving vision in inherited blindness
Report claims some blind people given an algae gene and goggles regained the ability to find and touch objects

headline: A molecule made by click chemistry was reported to restore vancomycin's ability to kill a drug-resistant superbug
summary: Chemists at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory reported that one of their click-chemistry molecules, made for an unrelated project, let the old antibiotic vancomycin kill vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium again in laboratory tests. The work is at the laboratory stage.
article_title: How an Old Antibiotic Can Now Kill a Drug-Resistant Superbug

headline: Antimicrobial peptides reconstructed from mammals that lived up to 160 million years ago were reported to be more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than modern human versions
summary: University of Oregon biologists rebuilt antimicrobial peptides from extinct mammal ancestors and tested them in the laboratory. Some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than the versions humans make today. The researchers present them as clues for designing treatments, not as a treatment.
article_title: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs

headline: The injection bepirovirsen was reported to be approved by the FDA as the first treatment offering a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B
summary: The FDA approved GSK's bepirovirsen, an injection given for about six months, for chronic hepatitis B. In two Phase 3 trials, 19% of treated adults still had no detectable viral protein 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, against under 1% on standard care. The article stresses that this is a functional cure, not clearance of the virus.
article_title: Breakthrough hepatitis B drug offers 'functional cure' for first time

headline: An AI-designed bacteriophage was reported by the startup that made it to have treated one patient's bacterial infection
summary: The startup Radical Numerics said it used AI to design a virus that attacks a patient's bacteria and that the infection was treated successfully. It gave no clinical details and the account was self-published, not peer reviewed. A microbiologist quoted in the article is sceptical.
article_title: Startup Deploys AI-Engineered Virus on Human Patient
California startup says it has injected AI-designed virus into humans for first time

headline: The once-weekly nasal spray INNA-051 was reported to prime the nose's antiviral defences against colds, flu, RSV and coronaviruses
summary: ENA Respiratory's dry-powder nasal spray is designed to prime the nose's own antiviral defences instead of targeting one virus, and the US Department of Defense has put nearly US$10 million into it. The company says it lowers viral load and does not block infection. A Phase 2a community study is under way in the USA.
article_title: Why the US is betting millions on this Aussie antiviral nasal spray
promise: A first trial in people with asthma is due to start in early 2027

headline: A single injection of donor stromal cells, rexlemestrocel-L, was reported to be in the final stage of a Phase 3 trial for chronic low back pain
indication: Chronic low back pain from degenerative disc disease
summary: Mesoblast said all 350 patients in its pivotal, sham-controlled Phase 3 trial have received either the cell injection or a sham injection. The main measure is pain at 12 months. The article says earlier results suggested up to a year of relief.
article_title: 'Blockbuster' one-shot low back pain drug in the home stretch of final test
promise: The trial's result will be known by mid-2027

headline: CAR-T cell therapy was reported to restore function in some people with stiff person syndrome in an early study
summary: Mayo Clinic neurologists gave CAR-T cell therapy, a treatment already used in cancer, to people with stiff person syndrome in an early study published in JAMA Neurology. Some patients who had needed help with daily tasks regained function and returned to work. The researchers say it is not yet known whether the gains last.
article_title: Medical breakthrough offers hope to people with same stiff person syndrome as Céline Dion

headline: The daily pill baxdrostat was reported to keep blood pressure lower for up to two years after patients with primary aldosteronism stopped taking it
summary: In a small study published in the New England Journal of Medicine, 14 patients took baxdrostat for 6 to 12 months. Their blood pressure stayed lower for up to two years after stopping, and just under a quarter came off all treatment with normal readings. NICE is assessing the drug.
article_title: New drug could be cure for common cause of high blood pressure
promise: Could be available through the NHS in 2027

headline: A gene therapy infused into the brain was reported to cut seizures by more than 90% in three adults with drug-resistant epilepsy
intervention: Gene therapy delivered by an engineered virus to seizure-triggering neurons, combined with a drug
summary: Three adults with long-standing drug-resistant epilepsy had an engineered virus infused into the part of the brain where their seizures start, in a trial published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Their monthly seizures fell by more than 90%. The researchers will follow the three long term and are preparing larger trials.
article_title: Experimental gene therapy on human brain reduces epileptic seizures by 90%

headline: Heart muscle cells grown from patients' own reprogrammed cells were reported to improve heart function in nine of ten patients with severe heart failure
intervention: Injection of heart muscle cells derived from the patient's own induced pluripotent stem cells
summary: At Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital, cells from ten patients were reprogrammed into stem cells, turned into heart muscle cells and injected into damaged areas of the heart. Nine of the ten showed improved heart function at 12 months, against 60% of ten control patients who had bypass surgery. The article gives no timeline for larger trials.
article_title: Chinese stem cell therapy reverses heart failure in 90% of patients, landmark trial finds
Chinese stem cell therapy reverses heart failure in 90% of patients, landmark trial finds

headline: A coronary sinus reducer implant was reported to cut chest pain significantly in three quarters of patients with refractory angina
summary: A study of the coronary sinus reducer, an implant fitted at the Royal Brompton hospital, found a significant fall in chest pain in 75% of patients. One patient fitted in 2021 went from five attacks a week to one every week or two. The article says further trials and NHS approval are still needed.
article_title: ‘An amazing relief’: implant offers hope for those with refractory angina

headline: A wireless implant that breaks down blood glucose was reported to normalise blood sugar in diabetic, obese mice
intervention: Wireless under-the-skin implant with an electrically powered glucose-degrading catalyst
summary: ETH Zurich researchers reported in Science that their implant brought blood sugar back to normal in diabetic, obese mice within 60 to 90 minutes of being switched on, and the animals lost up to 10% of body weight over six weeks. Outside experts said safety questions come first. The team plans tests in pigs and sheep before any human trial.
article_title: Drug-free diabetes implant offers ‘promising’ future for patients, say scientists
Scientists invent implant that can transform sugar in the blood to treat type 2 diabetes

headline: The daily pill solengepras was reported to cut daily 'off' time in Parkinson's disease by about 37 minutes more than placebo
indication: Motor symptoms ('off' time) in Parkinson's disease
summary: A randomised, placebo-controlled trial of solengepras in 341 patients in the US, Europe, the UK and Australia found that the higher dose reduced daily 'off' time by about 37 minutes more than placebo. The company, Cerevance, will take the results to the FDA to decide next steps.
article_title: Major Parkinson’s breakthrough as new pill offers hope of treating symptoms and has fewer side-effects
promise: The company says the pill could be prescribed within three years

headline: A genetically modified pig kidney was reported to have kept a man with kidney failure off dialysis for a record nine months
summary: A 66-year-old man with kidney failure, treated at Massachusetts General Hospital, lived for nine months without dialysis on a gene-edited pig kidney, the longest reported so far. Experts quoted in the article describe it as a possible bridge for people waiting a long time for a human kidney and call for more research.
article_title: Genetically modified pig kidney keeps man alive for record nine months
Pig kidney works for a record 271 days inside the body of American patient
Man given genetically modified pig kidney for nine months in world first

headline: A transplant of a teenager's own frozen testicular tissue was reported as the first in the UK, in the hope of restoring fertility after chemotherapy
intervention: Transplant of the patient's own previously frozen testicular tissue
summary: NHS surgeons in Edinburgh put testicular tissue, frozen three years earlier, back into a 19-year-old in the hope that it will produce sperm. It is the first such procedure in the UK and the second reported worldwide. It is not yet known whether it will work.
article_title: Teenager becomes first person to have testicular tissue transplant in UK
Frozen testicular tissue transplant offers hope of restoring fertility
Frozen testicular tissue transplanted in bid to restore fertility after chemotherapy

headline: A single dose of cabamiquine with pyronaridine was reported to be effective against malaria in an early trial
summary: An early-stage trial in adults and teenagers tested a single dose of cabamiquine, a drug discovered at the University of Dundee, combined with the existing antimalarial pyronaridine. It was effective with a favourable safety profile. The findings support larger trials, including in children.
article_title: Single dose malaria drug could simplify treatment worldwide in medical breakthrough
Big potential breakthrough for Parkinson's treatment as scientists 'thrilled'
Major Parkinson’s breakthrough as new pill offers hope of treating symptoms and has fewer side-effects

headline: Surgery linking neck lymphatic vessels to veins was reported as a possible way to drain proteins linked to dementia, with trials under way
summary: The article relays a report on a procedure that connects lymphatic vessels in the neck to veins, in the hope of draining waste proteins linked to dementia. It was offered widely in China, then restricted to clinical studies over doubts about safety and evidence. More than 20 trials are running there, and experts quoted say the idea is plausible but the publicity has run ahead of the evidence.
article_title: Dementia could be 'REVERSED' as surgery 'flushes out toxic proteins' from brain

headline: A microneedle skin stamp coated with peanut protein was reported to be in an early safety trial for peanut allergy
intervention: Microneedle skin stamp coated with peanut protein
summary: Allergists at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta are testing a small steel stamp coated with tiny doses of peanut protein, pressed on the forearm for about three minutes each week, with the dose rising as tolerated. The trial is an early study of safety and tolerability. The article gives no results.
article_title: The end of peanut allergies? First-of-its-kind 'stamp' is treating 'big problem'

headline: Blocking small blood vessels around the knee was reported to give lasting pain relief to about 80% of patients with knee osteoarthritis
summary: In a study of 194 people with knee osteoarthritis, doctors blocked excess small blood vessels around the knee with dissolving gelatin particles, guided by X-ray. About 80% reported a meaningful reduction in pain that lasted at least a year. The article presents it as a possible alternative to knee replacement.
article_title: Knee treatment without surgery offers lasting pain relief for 80% of arthritis patients, study finds

headline: The pill ATR-258 was reported to add muscle and leg strength in 13 overweight men over eight weeks without exercise
summary: In a first study in people at the University of Copenhagen, 13 overweight men took the tablet daily for eight weeks. They gained roughly 800 g of muscle and about 13% in leg strength while losing a little weight overall. The article says development is at an early stage and the aim is to protect muscle in people taking GLP-1 drugs.
article_title: New pill builds muscles 'as good as gym' without working out

headline: The injection CBL-514 was reported to cut visceral fat by about 12% after 12 weeks in Phase 2 trials
summary: The article reports two Phase 2 trials of CBL-514, an injection designed to destroy fat cells, in which visceral fat measured by MRI fell by about 12% on average after 12 weeks of injections. It suggests this could make weight regain less likely, which has not been tested.
article_title: New fat jab causes fat cells to 'self destruct' & stop dreaded weight re-gain

headline: Removal of the fallopian tubes was reported as a way to lower the risk of ovarian cancer by up to 80 per cent
summary: The Daily Mail reported that experts say removing the fallopian tubes could cut ovarian cancer risk by as much as 80 per cent, because most deadly ovarian cancers appear to start there. The procedure is already offered to high-risk women in a UK national research trial, and health bodies are encouraging doctors to offer it to women over 45 who are having other abdominal surgery. The article notes that 98 per cent of women will not develop ovarian cancer and calls the approach extreme.
article_title: 'Silent' ovarian cancer kills 4,000 British women every year, but a pioneering new treatment can slash the risk by 80%

headline: A once-weekly insulin injection was reported as approved for type 2 diabetes after trials showed similar control to daily insulin
summary: The Daily Mail reported that drug regulators have approved a long-acting insulin called insulin efsitora alfa (brand name Onswik) that can be injected once a week. Trials were reported to show it stabilises blood sugar about as well as daily insulin. NICE judged it good value, but the article says NHS England has not yet announced a nationwide roll-out.
article_title: Game-changing jab lets diabetics inject insulin once weekly, instead of daily

headline: Daraxonrasib was reported to have nearly doubled survival in advanced pancreatic cancer compared with standard chemotherapy
summary: A Daily Mail feature on a woman with stage 4 pancreatic cancer reported that the oral KRAS-blocking drug daraxonrasib extended survival in a trial published in the New England Journal of Medicine, from about 7 to 13 months versus standard chemotherapy. The article says side-effects were manageable. A charity leader quoted in it warns that few patients can access clinical trials.
article_title: Roxane was diagnosed with stage 4 pancreatic cancer that had spread to her liver. She thought she only had months left but now, two years later, she is alive

headline: Trontinemab is being tested in a Phase 3 trial to see whether it can prevent Alzheimer's disease in people without symptoms
summary: The Mirror reported that a Phase 3 trial called PrevenTRON will give trontinemab to about 1600 healthy adults aged 55 to 80 whose blood tests suggest early biological signs of Alzheimer's. The drug is given by infusion every three months and is intended to clear amyloid plaque build-up. A UK NHS trust is the first site in Europe to open the trial, which is sponsored by Roche; no results are reported yet.
article_title: Alzheimer's drug to be offered to people without symptoms to stop it developing

headline: Survodutide was reported to reduce belly and liver fat in a Phase 3 obesity trial
summary: The Mirror reported results from the Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 trial of survodutide, a once-weekly injection acting on glucagon and GLP-1 receptors. People with obesity but without type 2 diabetes lost up to 16.6 per cent of body weight over 76 weeks at the top dose, and a separate analysis found visceral fat down by up to 34 per cent and liver fat by up to 63.1 per cent. The article quotes a pharmacist saying the drug is still investigational and not approved, and notes the body-composition analysis involved a relatively small group.
article_title: New weight loss jab could 'target belly fat' as well as drop number on the scale

headline: TOFA was reported to cut body fat in obese mice and boost the effect of semaglutide and tirzepatide
summary: The Daily Mail reported that University of California Berkeley researchers found the 1970s compound TOFA makes cells burn fat for energy, in a study in mice published in Science Advances. Obese mice lost about 8.7 per cent of body weight in 24 days on TOFA alone, and much more when it was combined with low doses of semaglutide or tirzepatide, with almost all the loss being fat. The article stresses TOFA has not yet been tested in humans, so its safety profile is unknown.
article_title: The 1970s drug that turbocharges fat jabs - and cuts the side-effects

headline: Kudzu extract taken as needed was reported to reduce heavy-drinking days in people with alcohol use disorder in a placebo-controlled trial
indication: Binge drinking in alcohol use disorder
summary: The Daily Mail reported a three-month placebo-controlled trial of 120 US adults with alcohol use disorder who binged at least weekly, published in the American Journal of Psychiatry. Those taking 2000mg of kudzu extract when they felt urges drank on about a third fewer heavy-drinking days than the placebo group, with binge-drinking days falling from 2.15 to 1.42 a week. Researchers called the results exciting and a possible new tool for cutting back; the article notes the product pictured was not the one used in the study.
article_title: Scientists discover £20-a-month plant pill that can stop alcohol cravings: 'It turns off the reward feeling'

headline: Base editing was reported to convert the high-risk APOE4 gene to APOE3 in cells from Alzheimer's patients
summary: The Daily Mail reported that University of Bristol researchers converted the high-risk APOE4 gene into the lower-risk APOE3 variant in human immune cells derived from Alzheimer's patients, using a modified virus to deliver the editing tools. The team found very little unwanted DNA change in the cells. The article describes it as a technology that could one day be given as a one-off injection, so it is at the cell stage.
article_title: Gene switch therapy could prevent AND treat Alzheimer's

headline: An mRNA therapy that reawakens heart muscle cells was reported to improve heart function in mice after a heart attack
intervention: mRNA therapy activating Myc and Cyclin T1
indication: Heart muscle damage after heart attack and heart failure
summary: The Mirror reported a University of Cambridge study in mice, published in Nature Cardiovascular Research, in which short-lived mRNA injected into the heart temporarily activated two proteins (Myc and Cyclin T1) so heart muscle cells divided and helped repair damage. Treated mice had a stronger heartbeat and about 10 per cent more blood pumped per beat than mice given a mock treatment. The researchers say it is not a complete cure and describe it as an early step towards a possible heart failure treatment.
article_title: New heart attack experimental treatment discovers way to 'reawaken' damaged cells

headline: Orforglipron was reported to help adults with overweight or obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea in two trials
indication: Obstructive sleep apnoea in people with overweight or obesity
summary: The Daily Mail reported two clinical trials involving 712 adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea and a BMI of 27 or above, which found the once-daily pill orforglipron could be another treatment option alongside CPAP machines. The article notes the drug was approved by UK officials in August for weight management and type 2 diabetes but is not yet approved for sleep apnoea. A researcher quoted says it could be promising if approved for this use.
article_title: Weight-loss pill that could transform treatment for millions with a common 'snoring' condition linked to heart attacks and strokes

headline: A wrist-worn device that stimulates the median nerve was reported to reduce tics in people with Tourette syndrome
summary: A BBC News video report described a small wrist device developed at the University of Nottingham that delivers electrical pulses to the median nerve, which trials have shown can change activity in brain regions involved in movement control. It features a 15-year-old user who said tics stopped quickly. The piece does not give trial sizes or results, so the evidence is described only in general terms.
article_title: Tourette syndrome: The life-changing device helping to stop tics

headline: Trastuzumab deruxtecan was reported as newly available on the NHS for advanced HER2-low breast cancer
summary: The Mirror reported that NICE recommended Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) for routine NHS use in around 1000 people with HER2-low advanced breast cancer, after a two-year charity campaign. The drug is described as life-prolonging rather than curative. NHS England said it would make the treatment available to eligible patients immediately.
article_title: Women with advanced breast cancer from today can now get a life-extending drug on the NHS
